body.text: [USE ONE OF THE TWO OPENINGS BELOW. Wis. Stat. § 805.17(3) applies ONLY to findings after a trial to the court. Citing it to reconsider a summary judgment ruling or a non-final order is wrong. *Teff v. Unity Health Plans Ins. Corp.*, 2003 WI App 115.]

Plaintiff [NAME], pro se, respectfully moves this Court to reconsider its [DATE] Order [describing it]. That Order is non-final, and this Court “has the inherent authority to reconsider a nonfinal ruling any time prior to the entry of the final order or judgment.” *Teff v. Unity Health Plans Ins. Corp.*, 2003 WI App 115, ¶ 57. Reconsideration is warranted because the Order rests on [a manifest error of law / a manifest error of fact / newly discovered evidence]. *Koepsell's Olde Popcorn Wagons, Inc. v. Koepsell's Festival Popcorn Wagons, Ltd.*, 2004 WI App 129, ¶ 44. This motion does not re-argue the underlying motion, and it does not introduce evidence that could have been offered the first time.

Plaintiff [NAME], pro se, respectfully moves this Court under Wis. Stat. § 806.07(1)([letter]) for relief from the [Judgment/Order] entered [DATE], on the ground of [the statutory ground, in the statute's words]. [Explain timeliness: all grounds require a reasonable time; grounds (1)(a) and (c) also have a one-year limit; a ground under (1)(b) must comply with § 805.16. Verify the specific ground and deadline under § 806.07(2).]
I. [The specific error, stated as a proposition.]
[Identify precisely what the Court held, why it is error, and what authority controls. Do not re-argue.]

WHEREFORE, Plaintiff respectfully requests that the Court [vacate / amend] its [DATE] [Order/Judgment] and [specific relief], and grant such other and further relief as the Court deems just and proper.

[Calendar the appeal deadline from the ORIGINAL judgment. A reconsideration motion that merely re-argues does not extend it, and its denial is not separately appealable. *Silverton Enters. v. General Cas. Co.*, 143 Wis. 2d 661 (Ct. App. 1988); § 806.07(2).]
